title: Agentic Bug Reproduction for Effective Automated Program Repair at Google
datasets: 80 human-reported production bugs from Google internal GITS; 2025 version counts 80 (the cited related study later has 78 due infrastructure changes). Seven languages: Java, C++, Go, Python, Kotlin, Dart and TypeScript. Bug reports, ground-truth buggy files, fixed CLs and manually written oracle BRTs are internal/private. Defects4J and SWT-Bench are related-work references only, not experimental datasets.
task: Generate bug reproduction tests from issue reports in Google internal repositories, then study whether generated BRTs help Google’s internal APR (Passerine) and rank generated fixes via Ensemble Pass Rate.
input_setting: BRT Agent receives GITS issue title/description and buggy file contents; it can search/read internal repository files, edit test files with a Google-code-finetuned model, and execute Bazel tests. LIBRO additionally receives the ground-truth test file as context. The ground-truth fix/oracle is withheld from generation but used to evaluate F→P plausibility. For RQ2, selected plausible BRTs are fed to Passerine; the paper explicitly describes this as an upper bound because plausibility was determined using the ground-truth fix.
author_artifact_url: No public BRT Agent implementation or dataset URL identified; paper describes proprietary Google GITS, code_search, Bazel infrastructure, fine-tuned Gemini and Passerine.
author_relationship_evidence: The paper explicitly situates the system, data and infrastructure inside Google and describes an internal model fine-tuned on Google code. Exact-title/code searches found the arXiv paper and secondary indexes but no author code/data repository; the only GitHub links in references are unrelated tools/dependencies (e.g. Aider and sanitizers).
source_commit_or_archive: No public implementation, frozen benchmark, data archive, or repository snapshot located. Internal Google GITS issues and proprietary code-editing model/toolchain are unavailable; referenced LIBRO/SWT-Bench/Aider code is not the paper’s implementation.
license: The arXiv manuscript declares CC BY 4.0. No software/data license can be verified because no author artifact or internal dataset is public.
exact_models: A Gemini model fine-tuned on Google internal code for LIBRO/code editing; exact model ID, revision, and weights are not disclosed/public.
A publicly available Gemini model for BRT Agent reasoning; paper does not give a pinned public model identifier/revision.
Gemini for Passerine runs and Gemini-as-judge; configs are temperature 0.2/top-p 0.95 for Passerine, 20 runs/bug.
Adapted LIBRO uses temperature 0.7/top-p 0.95, 50 runs/bug; BRT Agent uses temperature 0.2/top-p 0.95 for reasoning and code edit, 20 runs/bug, maximum 25 steps/run.
weights_status: Critical code-editing Gemini weights are fine-tuned on Google internal code and not publicly available. Public reasoning Gemini identity is unspecified; no reproducible model snapshot or artifact verified.
evaluation_route: Read all 10,291 extracted words of arXiv v2 including sections 1–8 and references. On 80 internal Google bugs BRT Agent reaches 85% candidate and 28% plausible rates, vs LIBRO 41%/10%; 86% of plausible generated patches pass manual validity criteria, while 11% modify existing tests and are invalid. RQ2 on 23 selected cases finds Passerine plausible fixes 17/23 with a generated BRT vs 13/23 without (upper-bound selection based on known ground truth); plausible-fix probability when BRT used is 33% vs 2%. EPR ranks a plausible patch first in 70% of candidate pools of 20. No public task manifest/source/model route exists and no code/model run was attempted.
blockers: The 80 GITS bug reports, buggy/fixed Google source trees, oracle BRTs and expected outputs are proprietary; no data package found.
Core code_search, Bazel test execution, test conventions and Passerine are internal Google infrastructure.
The code-editing model is fine-tuned on Google internal code and not public; the public Gemini reasoning model is not pinned by exact ID/revision.

The paper’s headline results cannot be reproduced on Defects4J or SWT-Bench directly: those are related-work baselines/context, not this experiment’s dataset; adapting the agent to those datasets would be a new implementation/experiment.
concept_fit: Very high task alignment for actual bug-reproduction tests: defines BRT with Fail-to-Pass behavior and discusses root-cause usefulness; issue report and buggy source are inputs, while fixed-version oracle validates the test. But it provides no explicit root-cause taxonomy or tracked semantic-concept representation; its central agent is proprietary and cross-language. Strong comparator for task definition, BRT plausibility, test validity, and separation of candidate F→X from validated F→P.
recommendation: Use as a key related-work comparator and source of evaluation protocol distinctions (candidate vs plausible BRT, manual validity, APR utility and fix-ranking EPR). Do not select as a reproducible implementation baseline: all data, core infrastructure, trained code model and APR system are internal. For our own evaluation, use public SWT-Bench/Defects4J tasks with an independently approved implementation and report that as a new adaptation, not a reproduction of Google results.
supporting_locations: Full text SHA-256 82e45e3fc09fbfde87a67322b519fe54af82869a3faf91796b6056ebef7e1b21; all 10,291 extracted words reviewed.
Sections 2.1 and 5.1 define F→P and the private 80-bug Google GITS corpus; §5.1 notes seven languages and internal bug/fix/test records.
Sections 4.1–4.2 describe private code search, Bazel, Gemini fine-tuning and ReAct-style agent.
Sections 6.1–6.3 report generation, manual-validity, Passerine and EPR results; §5.2.2 calls RQ2 an upper bound due ground-truth-based BRT selection.
